paragraphs: Here's what I see, friend. Jesus walks beside two sad, confused followers, and He starts by asking what they're discussing and letting them tell it all (Luke 24:17-24). Then He opens the Scriptures. Beginning with Moses and all the Prophets, "He explained to them what was written in all the Scriptures about Himself" (Luke 24:27).

Now look at the sadness on that road, because they said, "we were hoping," and they had the facts right: the cross, the third day, the empty tomb (Luke 24:20-24). But facts alone left them stuck, so Jesus asked, "Was it not necessary for the Christ to suffer these things and then to enter His glory?" (Luke 24:26). The hard part was never a mistake. It was part of what the Scriptures said all along, and that's good news for any baker who's ever been confused.

And watch what happens after, because they said, "Were not our hearts burning within us as He spoke with us on the road and opened the Scriptures to us?" (Luke 24:32). God's Word does that, friend. It warms you up better than my ovens do, and I'd know, I've got SIX of them. So keep opening the Scriptures, keep asking Jesus to stay with you, and when your heart burns, go tell somebody, just like these two did.
